# STM32H743 Nano FC + 4-in-1 80A ESC: System Architecture Model (Job #23)

**Scope and assumptions:** No MOSFET part number, battery voltage, or board stack-up was specified. All equations are therefore given in parametric form first, then evaluated with representative values that are clearly marked. Before release, replace every value marked **[ASSUMED]** with the actual datasheet or measured figure.

**Architectural note:** In a 4-in-1 ESC, the 48 kHz PWM is generated by the ESC's own MCUs, typically AT32F421 or STM32G071 running AM32 or BLHeli_32. The H743 generates only DShot600 frames and decodes the bi-directional telemetry. The thermal and switching losses therefore belong to the ESC power stage, while DMA and timer allocation belongs to the H743.

---

## 1. Operating Point Definitions

| Symbol | Meaning | Value |
|---|---|---|
| V_bus | Battery voltage (6S full) | 25.2 V |
| I_burst | Per-channel DC burst current | 80 A |
| f_sw | ESC PWM frequency | 48 kHz |
| R_ds25 | MOSFET R_ds(on) at 25 °C, V_gs = 10 V | 0.80 mΩ **[ASSUMED]** |
| α | R_ds(on) temperature coefficient | 0.005 /K **[ASSUMED]** |
| T_j | Design junction temperature | 110 °C |
| Q_g / Q_gs2 / Q_gd | Gate charges | 60 / 8 / 10 nC **[ASSUMED]** |
| Q_oss, Q_rr | Output and reverse-recovery charge | 50 nC, 40 nC **[ASSUMED]** |
| V_plateau | Miller plateau voltage | 4.5 V |
| V_drv, R_g,tot | Gate drive voltage and total gate resistance | 10 V, 5 Ω on / 4 Ω off |
| t_dead | Dead time per edge | 100 ns |
| V_f | Body diode forward voltage at 80 A | 0.8 V |
| R_cu | PCB copper and solder per current path | 0.30 mΩ **[ASSUMED]** |

## 2. Conduction Loss Model

**Temperature-adjusted on-resistance:**

R_ds(T_j) = R_ds25 · [1 + α(T_j − 25)]
→ 0.80 mΩ × (1 + 0.005 × 85) = **1.14 mΩ**

**Current path:** For 6-step (trapezoidal) or FOC with complementary (synchronous) PWM, current flows through one high-side and one low-side switch in series at any instant. Over a PWM period on the switched leg:

- P_HS = D · I_ph² · R_ds(T)
- P_LS,sync = (1 − D) · I_ph² · R_ds(T)
- The sum is I_ph² · R_ds(T), independent of D.

Adding the static leg gives the per-channel conduction loss:

P_cond = I_ph² · 2R_ds(T_j) + I_ph² · R_cu

**Phase versus DC current:** I_ph ≈ I_DC / D. At burst, full throttle gives D ≈ 0.95–1, so I_ph ≈ 80–84 A. Use 80 A as the baseline. At partial throttle, the same DC current means higher phase current, so the conduction loss scales as I_DC² / D.

**Evaluation at 80 A:**
- MOSFETs: 80² × 2 × 1.14 mΩ = **14.6 W**
- Copper: 80² × 0.30 mΩ = **1.9 W**

**Self-consistency check:** R_ds depends on T_j, which depends on P. Iterate the following until it converges, which typically takes 2–3 iterations:

T_j = T_a + P_tot(T_j) · Z_th(t)

## 3. Switching Loss Model at 48 kHz

**Gate currents:**
- I_g,on = (V_drv − V_pl) / R_g,on = 5.5 / 5 = 1.1 A
- I_g,off = V_pl / R_g,off = 4.5 / 4 = 1.125 A
